parsed.explanation: No trans criminalisation, no universal-exposure measure: bathroom access protected, foreign documents face no documented friction, and the state protects rather than targets. Positives are substantial: employment discrimination covers gender identity, an active national action plan, Pride backed by government ministers, prosecutions of anti-LGBT assaults (2023 bar attack charged; 2022 trans murder drew a 12-year sentence with provocation rejected). Negatives: no hate-crime/hate-speech protection for gender identity, LGR still requires diagnosis, and social caution runs above regional averages (40% avoid locations fearing assault; first of 30 for hiding LGBTIQ at work) — friction/hostility signals, though LGBTIQ-wide and partly stale. One killing with a strong state response is not a pattern. Custody and border placement are open questions, not exposures. Net: functioning visitor-facing protection with real but non-pervasive social friction.
